summary: LTP subscriptions on two equities: an LTP packet becomes an LTP frame with its trade time in epoch ms; a binary frame carrying two packets back to back serves both instruments, where the web decodes only the first.

notes: The query carries x_jwt_token (paytm_websocket.py:232); subscriptions are JSON arrays of preferences.

deviations.reason: The web passes Paytm's trade time on in epoch seconds; WebSocket times are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md, CLAUDE.md), so a client reading ltt as ms on the web lands in January 1970. The desktop sends milliseconds.

The web's client decodes only the first packet of a binary frame (paytm_websocket.py:101-108, _parse_binary_data reads byte 0's packet), so a second packet in the same frame is lost; the desktop cuts every packet by its code's size (whether Paytm sends packets back to back is not verified live, audit RB-14).
